HOW TO RESTORE FROZEN-PLAIN
==========================================================
This package is stored UNENCRYPTED — no passphrase or key needed.
The payload file FROZEN-PLAIN.tar is a plain POSIX tar.

You need exactly two ubiquitous open-source programs:
  par2  (github.com/Parchive/par2cmdline)  - repair
  tar   (POSIX standard, preinstalled)     - extract

1) VERIFY / REPAIR:
     par2 verify FROZEN-PLAIN.tar.par2
     par2 repair FROZEN-PLAIN.tar.par2      (only if verify fails)
2) EXTRACT all, or one file (tar reads it directly, no gpg step):
     tar -xf FROZEN-PLAIN.tar
     tar -xf FROZEN-PLAIN.tar path/to/one/file

Integrity (SHA256):  payload 44f94b21442b699d3722730698976b9dbb545f5c54e763d486466e1cf0185f56
Full file list: FROZEN-PLAIN.manifest.json
No compression anywhere — extracted bytes are the originals.
==========================================================

WINDOWS — the tar built into Windows writes each file name in the system's
code page. A name that code page cannot hold (Japanese on a Western system,
for example) is refused with "unreadable filename", and the other files are
restored. The package keeps every name as UTF-8: to restore those files too,
extract FROZEN-PLAIN.tar with a tar that keeps Unicode names, such as 7-Zip
(7z x FROZEN-PLAIN.tar).
